weeks.title: Complex number fundamentals
objectives: Identify real and imaginary components and j powers.
Convert rectangular, polar and exponential forms with correct quadrants.
Explain equivalent angles and plot the same vector in different forms.

stages.title: The imaginary unit
stages.text: j²=-1 extends real arithmetic. Powers repeat every four: 1,j,-1,-j. A negative exponent follows the same cycle because j is nonzero.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Coordinates and quadrants
stages.text: In a+jb, a is the horizontal real coordinate and b the vertical imaginary coordinate. Magnitude is distance from the origin, never a signed length.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Phase and units
stages.text: Use atan2(b,a); atan(b/a) loses quadrant information and fails when a=0. The zero vector has no unique argument. A full revolution changes the phase representation but not the number.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Equivalent representations
stages.text: Euler links a rotating unit vector to a complex exponential. Polar and exponential representations use the same magnitude and phase. Explicitly label degrees or radians.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Try and explain
stages.text: Move the vector across an axis. Predict which component changes sign and which quadrant contains the result. Explain why adding a full turn changes neither component.
stages.math: theta and theta+2*pi give the same vector
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

weeks.title: Complex operations, De Moivre and impedance
objectives: Operate on complex numbers in appropriate forms.
Find and verify all nth roots.
Apply phasor arithmetic to ideal series and parallel impedances.

stages.title: Choose an efficient form
stages.text: Addition and subtraction combine rectangular components. Multiplication distributes with j²=-1. Polar multiplication multiplies magnitudes and adds phases.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Division and conjugates
stages.text: Multiply by the conjugate to obtain a real denominator. A zero denominator is undefined. Reciprocal magnitude inverts and phase negates.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Powers and roots
stages.text: De Moivre scales phase for integer powers. Roots reverse the operation, but a nonzero complex number has n distinct nth roots. Include every k, not only the principal root.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Phasor circuits
stages.text: Ideal linear sinusoidal steady state uses RMS phasors at one common frequency. Resistance is real and reactance imaginary. This calculation is a mathematical model of an AC circuit.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Verify physically and algebraically
stages.text: Multiply each root back to the nth power. In a circuit check KVL for series or KCL for parallel and retain ohms, volts and amperes. Zero denominators require separate analysis.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

weeks.title: Quadratic equation fundamentals
objectives: Solve pure, incomplete and full quadratic equations.
Interpret discriminants and repeated, irrational or nonreal roots.
Check solutions in the original equation.

stages.title: Put the equation in standard form
stages.text: Expand brackets and move every term to one side before reading a,b,c. The quadratic coefficient must be nonzero. Incomplete equations can be easier to solve directly.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Factoring and zero product
stages.text: A product is zero when at least one factor is zero. A repeated factor gives one distinct solution with multiplicity two. Never divide by x without checking x=0.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Complete the square
stages.text: Divide by the leading coefficient, then add the square of half the linear coefficient to both sides. This transforms the equation without losing roots.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Quadratic formula and discriminant
stages.text: A positive discriminant gives two distinct real roots, zero gives one repeated real root, and a negative discriminant gives two conjugate nonreal roots. Keep exact radicals when requested.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Substitute to check
stages.text: Evaluate the original left and right sides for every candidate. The sign before a square root creates two candidates, unless the square root is zero.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

weeks.title: Advanced quadratics and applications
objectives: Reduce rational, radical and higher-power equations to quadratics.
Reject extraneous roots and preserve denominator restrictions.
Use physically meaningful roots and quadratic extrema.

stages.title: Original domains first
stages.text: Record excluded denominator zeros before multiplying or cancelling. A cancelled factor does not restore an input that was originally undefined.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Squaring is not reversible
stages.text: Isolate a radical and record its nonnegative side. Squaring can create a candidate with the wrong sign. Only substitution in the original unsquared equation decides validity.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Substitution and division
stages.text: For even powers use u=x², solve the quadratic in u, and recover both signs for positive u. A known polynomial root allows division by x-r; solve the remaining factor as well.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Systems and engineering
stages.text: Substitute one relation into the other, then check both equations. Construct positive dimensions or resistances first when building a model. Algebraic negative roots may not describe a physical length.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Maxima and minima
stages.text: The vertex occurs at x=-b/(2a). Evaluate y there and check the physical domain endpoints if the model has a restricted interval.
stages.math: y=a*(x-h)²+k; sign(a) determines minimum or maximum
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

weeks.title: Analytical trigonometry and identities
objectives: Convert angle units and calculate exact special-angle values.
Apply reciprocal, quotient, Pythagorean, sum, difference, double and half-angle identities.
Preserve domains when proving an identity.

stages.title: The unit circle
stages.text: Cosine is the horizontal coordinate and sine the vertical coordinate on a unit circle. Quadrant signs come from coordinates, not memorized decimal approximations.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Related angles and reciprocals
stages.text: Sine is odd and cosine is even. Tangent is sine divided by cosine where cosine is nonzero. Reciprocal functions introduce their own denominator restrictions.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Addition and subtraction
stages.text: Expand with the angle-sum formulas before simplifying. For a difference, replace the second angle by its negative and track the signs.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Double and half angles
stages.text: Double-angle forms can trade products for sums or vice versa. A half-angle square root needs a sign chosen from the half-angle quadrant, not always the positive sign.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: A structured proof
stages.text: Transform one side using justified equalities until it matches the other. An identity holds throughout its common domain; checking a few angles is not a proof. State all denominator restrictions.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

weeks.title: Trigonometric equations, waves and phasors
objectives: Find complete solution sets in a specified interval.
Interpret and graph sinusoidal parameters with consistent units.
Combine equal-frequency waves and determine phase timing.

stages.title: All angle families
stages.text: An inverse sine gives only one principal value. Include the second angle family and complete turns, divide by any angle multiplier, then filter the requested interval.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Read a waveform
stages.text: Amplitude is nonnegative peak displacement from the offset. Period, frequency and angular frequency have different units. A phase angle is not a time shift.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: From function to graph
stages.text: Generate critical times from the angle, then evaluate the actual function. Label time in seconds and the vertical physical quantity. Plot at least a full period.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Combine equal frequencies
stages.text: Expand the target sine form and match coefficients. atan2 preserves the quadrant even when the sine coefficient is negative. Opposite equal waves can cancel completely.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Thresholds and timing
stages.text: Solve both angle families, retain times in the requested domain, and distinguish earliest positive from nonnegative. Positive phase leads the unshifted reference; lead time=phi/omega.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

weeks.title: Exponential functions and growth or decay
objectives: Read exponential domains, ranges and asymptotes.
Solve exponential equations and threshold problems.
Interpret RC models with correct physical labels and SI units.

stages.title: Growth and decay
stages.text: For y=A*exp(k*t), A>0, positive k gives growth and negative k decay. The mathematical domain is all real t and range is positive; elapsed physical time is often t≥0.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Inverse relationships
stages.text: Divide by the initial value before taking logarithms. A positive exponential cannot equal a nonpositive target over the reals.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Time constants
stages.text: For decay exp(-t/tau), tau must be positive. At one tau the remaining fraction is exp(-1); an ideal asymptote is approached, not reached at finite time.
stages.math: tau=RC for an ideal RC circuit; tau=L/R for an ideal RL circuit
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Correct circuit quantities
stages.text: A charging capacitor voltage rises toward the source while the series current decays. A discharging capacitor voltage and resistor-current magnitude decay. An RL step current rises on L/R.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Graph and check
stages.text: Change R or C to stretch time without changing the voltage asymptote. Check initial value, long-time value and unit conversions before interpreting the curve.
stages.math: R in ohms, C in farads, t and tau in seconds
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

weeks.title: Logarithms and decibels
objectives: Use log laws on valid domains and solve with substitution checks.
Convert bases and combine or expand logarithms.
Distinguish power and voltage gain formulas.

stages.title: Definition and domain
stages.text: A logarithm asks for an exponent. Its real argument must be positive and its base positive and unequal to one. Natural logs use base e; common logs use base ten.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Laws and change of base
stages.text: Products become sums, quotients differences, and powers coefficients on the stated positive domain. A log of a sum cannot be split into logs of its terms.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Solve and validate
stages.text: Write every argument restriction before combining logs. Algebra may give multiple roots, but each must satisfy the original arguments and equation.
stages.math: log_b(x-h)+log_b(x+h) has domain x>h for h>0
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Decibel gain
stages.text: Power gain uses ten times the common logarithm. RMS voltage gain uses twenty times the logarithm when equal positive resistive impedances are assumed. Negative gain means attenuation.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Invert a gain
stages.text: Exponentiate to recover a ratio. Keep the sign of gain and convert mW or mV consistently on both sides. Do not mix a power ratio with a voltage formula.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

weeks.title: Descriptive statistics and data
objectives: Calculate mean, median, all modes, quartiles and IQR.
Use the explicitly stated quartile convention.
Interpret generated measurements and frequency tables.

stages.title: Order and count
stages.text: Sort a copy of the observations. Retain repeated values because their frequencies affect the mean, median and quartiles. Count the observations before calculating.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Mean and frequency tables
stages.text: Arithmetic mean is total divided by count. For a frequency table multiply every distinct value by its count before summing.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Median and modes
stages.text: The median is the middle value for odd n and average of two middle values for even n. Return every value tied for greatest frequency. In this course all-unique data have no mode.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Quartile convention
stages.text: Use medians of the lower and upper halves. Include the central observation in both halves when n is odd. The worksheet states this rule because common conventions can differ.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Interpret measurements
stages.text: Mean summarizes center but does not describe every reading. Keep measurement units and precision; a repeated reading is not necessarily a mistake. Verify weighted totals against expanded data.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

weeks.title: Probability and comprehensive review
objectives: Count equally likely outcomes and use complements correctly.
Distinguish exactly, at least and replacement assumptions.
Combine fresh practice from all five units.

stages.title: Sample spaces
stages.text: Specify the experiment, then count ordered equally likely elementary outcomes. Dice sums are not equally likely. Probability lies from zero through one.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Dice and complements
stages.text: For n fair independent six-sided dice there are 6^n ordered face tuples. Enumerate the tuples matching a sum or event. Complementary events partition the entire sample space.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Coins: exactly versus at least
stages.text: For n independent fair tosses there are 2^n ordered strings. Exactly k heads selects one count; at least k includes every count k through n.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Cards and replacement
stages.text: Use a standard 52-card deck without jokers. Multiple draws explicitly state replacement. Without replacement, draw probabilities change; with replacement the original counts return.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example

stages.title: Comprehensive strategy
stages.text: For a mixed problem first identify its unit, domain, representation and units. Draw a diagram where useful, solve, and substitute or recount independently. Practice results do not enter official averages.
stages.interaction: predict, manipulate descriptor, explain, then compare generated worked example
